## Reverse-engineering agent evaluation

[↑ Contents](#contents)

- [**Humans vs. Machines: A Comparison With AI Agents in Software Reverse Engineering**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14960) - Compares human and LLM-agent understanding and navigation on the same static reverse-engineering challenges, then studies how binary representations consume context windows. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Samuele Doria et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.14960) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-humans-machines-sre/)</sub>
- [**Training Language Model Agents to Find Vulnerabilities with CTF-Dojo**](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/zhuo26c.html) - CTF-Dojo is an execution environment for training LLM agents on capture-the-flag tasks: 658 challenges from 50 competitions held between 2011 and 2025, taken from pwn.college's CTF Archive and containerized with Docker. <sub>ICML 2026 · Conference paper · Terry Yue Zhuo et al. · [PDF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v306/main/assets/zhuo26c/zhuo26c.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/amazon-science/CTF-Dojo) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-ctf-dojo/)</sub>
- [**Reveree: Diagnosing LLM Reverse-Engineering Agents**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01185) - Evaluates reverse-engineering agent traces through flag recovery, eight analysis milestones and action profiles. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Hadjer Benkraouda et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.01185v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-reveree/)</sub>
- [**The Next Challenge for Agentic Cybersecurity: A Realistic, Contamination-Free Reverse Engineering Benchmark**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11469) - Introduces SRE-Bench, with privately authored programs and protected binary variants, to study agent recovery of program semantics while reducing training-data contamination. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Jeremy Spence et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.11469) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-sre-bench/)</sub>
- [**Automatically Attacking Software Reverse Engineering AI Agents**](https://papers.academic-conferences.org/index.php/eccws/article/view/4597) - A proof of concept for indirect prompt injection against Cline/GhidraMCP binary-analysis agents. <sub>ECCWS 2026 · Conference paper · Brian Crawford et al. · [PDF](https://papers.academic-conferences.org/index.php/eccws/article/download/4597/4412/17540) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-attacking-re-ai-agents/)</sub>
- [**CrackMeBench: Binary Reverse Engineering for Agents**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10597) - Evaluates agents on executable-checked CrackMe tasks: infer validation logic from binaries and submit an accepted input or artifact, while recording tool use, time, and scoring attempts. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Isaac David et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.10597) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-crackmebench/)</sub>
- [**Towards LLM-Resistant Software Protection: Agent Failure Patterns in CTF Reverse Engineering**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/auto-draft-657/) - Runs Claude Code, Codex CLI and ChatGPT-5.2 Pro on 24 crackme-style challenges selected from 15 international CTF events held in 2025, and attributes their failures to stages of an Observe–Comprehend–Plan loop and to three protection effects: concealment, complication and misdirection. <sub>Workshop on Binary Analysis Research (BAR) 2026 · Conference paper · Ryutaro Nishizaka et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/bar2026-58.pdf) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-llm-resistant-protection/)</sub>
- [**ProgramBench: Can Language Models Rebuild Programs From Scratch?**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03546) - Evaluates black-box program reconstruction across 200 tasks: agents query an executable and read its documentation, then independently implement a codebase whose behavior is checked by generated tests. <sub>NeurIPS 2026 · Conference accepted · John Yang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.03546v1) · [Code](https://github.com/facebookresearch/ProgramBench) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-programbench/)</sub>
- [**Decompiling the Synergy: An Empirical Study of Human–LLM Teaming in Software Reverse Engineering**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/decompiling-the-synergy-an-empirical-study-of-human-llm-teaming-in-software-reverse-engineering/) - Studies how human analysts work with LLM assistance during static software reverse engineering. <sub>NDSS 2026 · Conference paper · Zion Leonahenahe Basque et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2026-f380-paper.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/mahaloz/dec-synergy-study) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-decompiling-synergy/)</sub>
- [**Cyber-Zero: Training Cybersecurity Agents without Runtime**](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/hash/f9f54762cbb4fe4dbffdd4f792c31221-Abstract-Conference.html) - Cyber-Zero synthesizes training trajectories for capture-the-flag (CTF) agents from public writeups instead of running the challenges. <sub>ICLR 2026 · Conference paper · Terry Yue Zhuo et al. · [PDF](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/file/f9f54762cbb4fe4dbffdd4f792c31221-Paper-Conference.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/amazon-science/Cyber-Zero) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-cyber-zero/)</sub>
- [**CREBench: Evaluating Large Language Models in Cryptographic Binary Reverse Engineering**](https://openreview.net/forum?id=tLYdf8hWJB) - Benchmarks cryptographic binary reverse engineering across algorithm recognition, key or IV extraction, wrapper reconstruction, and flag recovery using 432 controlled challenges. <sub>COLM 2026 · Conference paper · Baicheng Chen et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.03750v2) · [Code](https://github.com/wangyu-ovo/CREBench) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-crebench/)</sub>
- [**EnIGMA: Interactive Tools Substantially Assist LM Agents in Finding Security Vulnerabilities**](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/abramovich25a.html) - EnIGMA extends SWE-agent for capture-the-flag challenges with interactive agent tools that keep a gdb debugging session or a pwntools server connection open across turns, alongside decompile and disassemble commands, an LM summarizer for long outputs, and category-specific demonstrations and guidelines. <sub>ICML 2025 · Conference paper · Talor Abramovich et al. · [PDF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v267/main/assets/abramovich25a/abramovich25a.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/tree/v0.7) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-enigma/)</sub>
- [**Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models**](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/3e9412a9c1d93810ef3ef7825115016b-Abstract-Conference.html) - Cybench turns 40 professional-level capture-the-flag tasks from four competitions (HackTheBox Cyber Apocalypse 2024, SekaiCTF 2022–23, GlacierCTF and HKCert) into runnable agent tasks. <sub>ICLR 2025 · Conference paper · Andy K. Zhang et al. · [PDF](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/3e9412a9c1d93810ef3ef7825115016b-Paper-Conference.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/andyzorigin/cybench) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-cybench/)</sub>
- [**NYU CTF Bench: A Scalable Open-Source Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating LLMs in Offensive Security**](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/69d97a6493fbf016fff0a751f253ad18-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.html) - NYU CTF Bench packages 200 manually validated challenges from CSAW CTF qualifying and final rounds held between 2017 and 2023, spanning cryptography, forensics, pwn, reverse engineering, web and miscellaneous tasks, with challenge.json metadata and Docker images for server-side challenges. <sub>NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks · Conference paper · Minghao Shao et al. · [PDF](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/69d97a6493fbf016fff0a751f253ad18-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/NYU-LLM-CTF/NYU_CTF_Bench) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-nyu-ctf-bench/)</sub>

## Decompilation and symbol recovery

[↑ Contents](#contents)

- [**ICALL-BENCH: Benchmarking LLM Interprocedural Reasoning in Binary Programs**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37871v1) - ICALL-BENCH measures whether language models and agents can follow interprocedural meaning in compiled binaries, using indirect-call target recovery as the probe. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Shenglong Yao et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.37871v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-icall-bench/)</sub>
- [**BUSTA: Teaching Small Language Models to Reason About Binary Execution**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36288) - BUSTA trains small language models to infer input register values from an x86-64 basic block and desired output register state. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Ritika Poddar et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36288) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-busta/)</sub>
- [**VulDec: Vulnerability Detection in Binaries via Neural Decompilation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33716) - VulDec pairs real-world assembly and C code with CWE labels and uses neural decompilation to detect binary vulnerabilities. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Francesco Crescenzo Grasso et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.33716) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-vuldec/)</sub>
- [**Rethinking Neural Decompilation: Candidate Selection as the Hidden Bottleneck**](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-981-92-6837-5_38) - The paper compares methods for selecting LLM4Decompile's reconstructed code candidates and evaluates fine-tuning on an OLLVM-obfuscated binary dataset. <sub>ICICS 2026 · Conference paper · Felix Mächtle et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.02788) · [Code](https://github.com/UzL-ITS/rethinking-neural-decompilation) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-rethinking-neural-decompilation/)</sub>
- [**ATLAS: A Multi-Agent Framework for Lifting Binary to Canonical Compiler IR**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30877) - ATLAS lifts optimized disassembly to canonical LLVM IR using region-level retrieval and agents that iteratively repair IR with compiler diagnostics and runtime checks. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Xiaoao Zhu et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.30877) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-atlas/)</sub>
- [**VMSpec: A Decompiler-based Approach against Virtual Machine Obfuscation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29566) - VMSpec automatically builds VM processor specifications that let decompilers recover the behavior of VM-obfuscated programs. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Fabian Kilger et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.29566) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-vmspec/)</sub>
- [**ExeBench-FHD: Addressing Fidelity Issues in Decompiler Evaluation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28212) - The paper identifies nine fidelity issues in ExeBench and introduces ExeBench-FHD, adding assembly, data, wrapper and warning fields to improve LLM decompiler evaluation. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Akarsh Ashok et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.28212) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-exebench-fhd/)</sub>
- [**A Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Engine for Compilation-Free Patch Presence Testing**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27871) - SyLares converts source code and decompiled pseudocode into SMT-LIB equivalence queries, using an LLM to align code and Z3 to decide whether a patch is present. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Siyuan Li et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.27871) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-sylares/)</sub>
- [**Locate, Then Reason: End-to-End Patch Presence Testing in Stripped Binaries**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25071) - Locates patch-relevant code in stripped binaries using instruction-aligned retrieval and caller/callee context, then uses an LLM to screen candidate matches and compare patch-specific behavior with vulnerable and patched references. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Huaijin Wang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.25071v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-patchalign/)</sub>
- [**InterType: Breaking the Single-Function Barrier in Neural Binary Type Inference**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26906) - InterType adds caller-callee data flow to a Transformer for variable type recovery in stripped binaries. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Shan Wang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.26906) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-intertype/)</sub>
- [**Recall-Oriented Precise Binary-to-Source Function Matching**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23546) - BScout matches decompiled functions to a source corpus using chunked embeddings and inlining-aware training. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Junlin Li et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.23546v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-bscout/)</sub>
- [**Decoding What iOS Location Services Send to Apple: An LLM Is an Unreliable Analyst but a Useful Toolmaker**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21597) - Compares direct LLM recovery of Apple PBCodable schemas with an AI-written Extractor checked against compiled synthetic fixtures, published descriptors and captured traffic. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Douglas Leith · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.21597v1) · [Code](https://github.com/doug-leith/ios-protobuf-decoding) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-ios-protobuf-extractor/)</sub>
- [**SoK: Are LLMs Reliable at Source Code Recovery? A Taxonomy and Empirical Evaluation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11556) - This SoK organizes LLM-assisted source-recovery designs and separates compilation, readability, structural and behavioral metrics. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Varun Kohli et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.11556v1) · [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/decompbench-65CB/) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-sok-source-recovery-reliability/)</sub>

- [**Instruction Alignment for Binary Code Representation Learning**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3832783.3837516) - The paper adds instruction alignment as an auxiliary objective for binary code representation learning and evaluates its effect on function retrieval accuracy and similarity judgments. <sub>ASE '26 2026 · Conference paper · Huaijin Wang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.11766) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-instruction-alignment-for-binary-code-representation/)</sub>

- [**Decompiling Quantum Assembly into Structured Programs**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05012) - Quelle recovers library calls, loops, functions and symbolic parameters from compiled OpenQASM. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Pingchuan Ma et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.05012v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-quelle/)</sub>
- [**ASAP: Assembly-Source Aligned Pseudocode Refinement For Binary Decompilation**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06900) - ASAP aligns assembly and source representations during training, compresses assembly features into tokens, and supplies them alongside decompiler pseudocode to an LLM refiner. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Yujian Zhuang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.06900v1) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-asap-decompilation/)</sub>

- [**BinSlayer: accurate comparison of binary executables**](https://doi.org/10.1145/2430553.2430557) - BinSlayer combines BinDiff with Hungarian bipartite graph matching to compare binaries and computes a graph-edit-distance similarity metric. <sub>PPREW '13 2013 · Conference paper · Martial Bourquin et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/2430553.2430557) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-binslayer/)</sub>

Jacobson et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/2024569.2024571) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-labeling-library-functions-in-stripped-binaries/)</sub>

- [**Mapping kernel objects to enable systematic integrity checking**](https://doi.org/10.1145/1653662.1653729) - KOP maps dynamic kernel objects by resolving generic pointers, unions, and dynamic arrays. <sub>CCS '09 2009 · Conference paper · Martim Carbone et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/1653662.1653729) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-mapping-kernel-objects-to-enable-systematic/)</sub>
- [**A syntax-directed approach to inverse compilation**](https://doi.org/10.1145/1408800.1408926) - Describes a syntax-directed strategy for inverse compilation: translating machine-level programs into equivalent higher-level programs. <sub>ACM '74 1974 · Conference paper · Clifford R. Hollander · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/1408800.1408926) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-a-syntax-directed-approach-to-inverse-compilation/)</sub>

- [**Fuzzware: Using Precise MMIO Modeling for Effective Firmware Fuzzing**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity22/presentation/scharnowski) - Rehosts monolithic ARM Cortex-M firmware for fuzzing, using locally scoped symbolic execution to model memory-mapped I/O accesses and focus input mutations on values relevant to firmware logic. <sub>USENIX Security 2022 · Conference paper · Tobias Scharnowski et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec22-scharnowski.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/fuzzware-fuzzer/fuzzware) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-fuzzware/)</sub>
- [**A large-scale empirical analysis of the vulnerabilities introduced by third-party components in IoT firmware**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3533767.3534366) - FirmSec identifies third-party components and versions in IoT firmware using syntactic and control-flow features, then maps them to vulnerabilities. <sub>ISSTA '22 2022 · Conference paper · Binbin Zhao et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3533767.3534366) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmsec/)</sub>
- [**Reverse engineering and retrofitting robotic aerial vehicle control firmware using dispatch**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3498361.3538938) - DisPatch decompiles RAV firmware to recover controller functions and variables, then injects patches written in a DSL. <sub>MobiSys '22 2022 · Conference paper · Taegyu Kim et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3498361.3538938) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-reverse-engineering-and-retrofitting-robotic-aerial/)</sub>
- [**ECMO: Peripheral Transplantation to Rehost Embedded Linux Kernels**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3460120.3484753) - ECMO transplants peripheral drivers into embedded Linux kernels to boot firmware in QEMU. <sub>Proceedings of the 2021 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security · Conference paper · Muhui Jiang et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.14295) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-ecmo/)</sub>
- [**Jetset: Targeted Firmware Rehosting for Embedded Systems**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity21/presentation/johnson) - Jetset rehosts firmware only as far as an analyst-chosen goal address, such as the point where a fuzzer can inject input. <sub>USENIX Security 2021 · Conference paper · Evan Johnson et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec21-johnson.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/aerosec/jetset) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-jetset/)</sub>
- [**Automatic Firmware Emulation through Invalidity-guided Knowledge Inference**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity21/presentation/zhou) - µEmu emulates ARM Cortex-M microcontroller firmware without real hardware or hand-written peripheral models by symbolically executing the image with unknown peripheral registers as symbols. <sub>USENIX Security 2021 · Conference paper · Wei Zhou et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec21-zhou.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/MCUSec/uEmu/tree/c82fc0a36a28ab5f96001b0682adcf9783e20346) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-uemu/)</sub>
- [**SoK: Enabling Security Analyses of Embedded Systems via Rehosting**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3433210.3453093) - Systematizes rehosting: moving embedded firmware from its physical hardware into a virtual environment that models enough hardware behavior for dynamic analysis such as fuzzing and symbolic execution. <sub>ACM ASIA CCS 2021 · Conference paper · Andrew Fasano et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3433210.3453093) · [Code](https://github.com/rehosting/rehosting_sok) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-rehosting-sok/)</sub>
- [**Conware: Automated Modeling of Hardware Peripherals**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3433210.3437532) - Conware builds reusable software models of hardware peripherals from recordings of real firmware–peripheral interactions. <sub>ACM ASIA CCS 2021 · Conference paper · Chad Spensky et al. · [PDF](https://sites.cs.ucsb.edu/~chris/research/doc/asiaccs21_conware.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/ucsb-seclab/conware/tree/05dfdf5552d5c05dfca32137487fc8b3aadcd256) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-conware/)</sub>
- [**Snipuzz: Black-box Fuzzing of IoT Firmware via Message Snippet Inference**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.05445) - Snipuzz fuzzes IoT firmware as a client, using device responses to infer message snippets that guide mutations. <sub>ACM CCS 2021 · Conference accepted · Xiaotao Feng et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.05445) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-snipuzz/)</sub>
- [**DICE: Automatic Emulation of DMA Input Channels for Dynamic Firmware Analysis**](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9519398) - DICE adds DMA input emulation to microcontroller firmware emulators that model neither peripherals nor DMA controllers. <sub>IEEE S&amp;P 2021 · Conference paper · Alejandro Mera et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2007.01502v3) · [Code](https://github.com/RiS3-Lab/DICE-DMA-Emulation/tree/2b3b8c8b722abdbd7ff9e35fc7b02914fddf75df) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-dice/)</sub>
- [**Challenges in Firmware Re-Hosting, Emulation, and Analysis**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3423167) - Surveys firmware re-hosting tools and workflows, classifies popular works along five axes, and presents 28 challenges from firmware acquisition through post-emulation analysis. <sub>ACM Computing Surveys 2021 · Journal article · Christopher Wright et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3423167) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmware-rehosting-challenges/)</sub>
- [**From Library Portability to Para-rehosting: Natively Executing Microcontroller Software on Commodity Hardware**](https://doi.org/10.14722/ndss.2021.24308) - The paper uses a POSIX-based portable MCU and replaceable peripheral drivers to rehost MCU software for native execution and security testing on commodity hardware. <sub>Proceedings 2021 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium · Conference paper · Wenqiang Li et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.12867) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-para-rehosting/)</sub>
- [**FirmAE: Towards Large-Scale Emulation of IoT Firmware for Dynamic Analysis**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3427228.3427294) - Extends Firmadyne with empirically derived interventions for boot, networking, NVRAM, kernel behavior, and other runtime failures, enabling Linux router and IP-camera firmware web services to run for dynamic analysis. <sub>ACSAC 2020 · Conference paper · Mingeun Kim et al. · [PDF](https://syssec.kaist.ac.kr/pub/2020/kim_acsac2020.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/pr0v3rbs/FirmAE) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmae/)</sub>
- [**Device-agnostic Firmware Execution is Possible: A Concolic Execution Approach for Peripheral Emulation**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3427228.3427280) - Laelaps uses symbolic execution to infer the peripheral inputs firmware expects and steer its concrete execution without prior device knowledge. <sub>ACSAC '20 2020 · Conference paper · Chen Cao et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3427228.3427280) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-device-agnostic-firmware-execution-is-possible-a/)</sub>
- [**FirmXRay: Detecting Bluetooth Link Layer Vulnerabilities From Bare-Metal Firmware**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3372297.3423344) - FirmXRay statically analyzes bare-metal BLE firmware, identifying base addresses, data structures, and configuration values to detect link-layer vulnerabilities. <sub>CCS '20 2020 · Conference paper · Haohuang Wen et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3372297.3423344) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmxray/)</sub>
- [**P2IM: Scalable and Hardware-independent Firmware Testing via Automatic Peripheral Interface Modeling**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity20/presentation/feng) - P2IM emulates monolithic ARM Cortex-M firmware in a modified QEMU by classifying memory-mapped I/O registers as control-status, status, data or control-data during speculative execution runs and feeding fuzzer inputs through data registers and round-robin interrupts. <sub>USENIX Security 2020 · Conference paper · Bo Feng et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec20-feng.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/RiS3-Lab/p2im) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-p2im/)</sub>
- [**HALucinator: Firmware Re-hosting Through Abstraction Layer Emulation**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity20/presentation/clements) - HALucinator rehosts monolithic ARM Cortex-M firmware by identifying hardware-abstraction-library functions and replacing them with authored Python handlers and peripheral models. <sub>USENIX Security 2020 · Conference paper · Abraham A Clements et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec20-clements.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/embedded-sec/halucinator) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-halucinator/)</sub>
- [**On Manually Reverse Engineering Communication Protocols of Linux Based IoT Systems**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.11981) - Presents a manual framework for reverse engineering communication protocols in embedded Linux IoT systems. <sub>arXiv 2020 · Preprint · Kaizheng Liu et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2007.11981) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-manually-re-iot-protocols/)</sub>
- [**BaseSAFE: Baseband SAnitized Fuzzing through Emulation**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3395351.3399360) - BaseSAFE partially rehosts closed-source cellular baseband firmware for instrumented fuzzing and uses a sanitizing allocator to detect heap buffer overflows. <sub>Proceedings of the 13th ACM Conference on Security and Privacy in Wireless and Mobile Networks 2020 · Conference paper · Dominik Maier et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.07797) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-basesafe/)</sub>
- [**Frankenstein: Advanced Wireless Fuzzing to Exploit New Bluetooth Escalation Targets**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.09809) - Frankenstein emulates Bluetooth firmware dumps and fuzzes a virtual modem. <sub>USENIX Security 2020 · Conference accepted · Jan Ruge et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.09809) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-frankenstein/)</sub>
- [**FirmUp: Precise Static Detection of Common Vulnerabilities in Firmware**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3296957.3177157) - FirmUp matches known vulnerable procedures in stripped firmware binaries using procedure similarity and relationships among procedures. <sub>ACM SIGPLAN Notices 2018 · Journal article · Yaniv David et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3296957.3177157) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmup/)</sub>
- [**FirmUSB: Vetting USB Device Firmware using Domain Informed Symbolic Execution**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3133956.3134050) - FirmUSB uses USB protocol knowledge and symbolic execution to analyze firmware without source code. <sub>CCS '17 2017 · Conference paper · Grant Hernandez et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1708.09114) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmusb/)</sub>
- [**Scalable Graph-based Bug Search for Firmware Images**](https://doi.org/10.1145/2976749.2978370) - Genius converts binary control-flow graphs into numeric vectors and uses hashing to search firmware for similar vulnerable functions. <sub>CCS'16 2016 · Conference paper · Qian Feng et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/2976749.2978370) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-scalable-graph-based-bug-search-for-firmware/)</sub>
- [**Towards Automated Dynamic Analysis for Linux-based Embedded Firmware**](https://doi.org/10.14722/ndss.2016.23415) - Firmadyne crawls, extracts and emulates Linux-based firmware for network-connected commercial devices such as routers and IP cameras. <sub>NDSS 2016 · Conference paper · Daming D. Chen et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/towards-automated-dynamic-analysis-linux-based-embedded-firmware.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/firmadyne/firmadyne) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-firmadyne/)</sub>
- [**Automated Dynamic Firmware Analysis at Scale: A Case Study on Embedded Web Interfaces**](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03609) - The paper emulates firmware images and uses static and dynamic tools to find vulnerabilities in embedded web interfaces. <sub>arXiv 2015 · Preprint · Andrei Costin et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.03609) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-dynamic-firmware-analysis-at-scale/)</sub>
- [**Avatar: A Framework to Support Dynamic Security Analysis of Embedded Systems’ Firmwares**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss2014/ndss-2014-programme/avatar-framework-support-dynamic-security-analysis-embedded-systems-firmwares/) - Avatar runs embedded firmware in an instrumented emulator, S²E on QEMU, while forwarding memory-mapped I/O to the real device and injecting the device's interrupts back into the emulator, so firmware that depends on undocumented peripherals can still be analyzed dynamically. <sub>NDSS 2014 · Conference paper · Jonas Zaddach et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/02_3_1.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/avatarone/avatar-python) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-avatar/)</sub>

## Protocol inference and analysis

[↑ Contents](#contents)

- [**SEMPRE: Semantic-Aware Protocol Reverse Engineering via Consistency-Driven Joint Optimization**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31844) - SEMPRE uses dynamic analysis and LLM reasoning to recover hierarchical message fields, infer their types and roles, and refine field boundaries. <sub>arXiv 2026 · Preprint · Yihua Xu et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.31844) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-sempre/)</sub>
- [**Protocol Reverse Engineering via Deep Transfer Learning**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3797124) - Transfers field-boundary patterns from standardized protocol traces labeled by Tshark to poorly documented target protocols. <sub>Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering / FSE 2026 · Journal article · Yanyang Zhao et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3797124) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-transre/)</sub>
- [**RFCLLM: Evaluating LLMs' Reasoning Ability of Network Protocol State Machines**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13389) - Tests reasoning over protocol state machines using 1,482 questions across 16 protocols. <sub>Findings of EMNLP 2026 · Conference accepted · Anqi Chen et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.13389v1) · [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/rfcllm) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-rfcllm/)</sub>
- [**Recovering Process Variables from Industrial Network Traffic via Search-Based Optimization**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16403) - PVParser recovers process-variable layouts from industrial traffic and historian records. <sub>CCS 2026 · Conference accepted · Chuan Sheng et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.16403v2) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-pvparser/)</sub>
- [**ICEPRE: ICS Protocol Reverse Engineering via Data-Driven Concolic Execution**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3728982) - Infers message-field boundaries by following concrete message-guided paths through binary protocol parsers, then symbolically replaying them to extract byte-level data flow. <sub>Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (ISSTA 2025) · Journal article · Yibo Qu et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3728982) · [Code](https://github.com/QYbPtqyb/ICEPRE) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-icepre/)</sub>
- [**Unleashing the Power of LLM to Infer State Machine From the Protocol Implementation**](https://doi.org/10.1109/IWQoS65803.2025.11143461) - ProtocolGPT infers protocol state machines from implementation source code with a retrieval-augmented LLM. <sub>IWQoS 2025 · Conference paper · Haiyang Wei et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.00393v4) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-protocolgpt/)</sub>
- [**BinPRE: Enhancing Field Inference in Binary Analysis Based Protocol Reverse Engineering**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3658644.3690299) - Infers protocol-message field boundaries and semantics from instrumented server binaries and input messages. <sub>ACM CCS 2024 · Conference paper · Jiayi Jiang et al. · [PDF](https://tingsu.github.io/files/ccs24-BinPRE.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/ecnusse/BinPRE) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-binpre/)</sub>
- [**DynPRE: Protocol Reverse Engineering via Dynamic Inference**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/dynpre-protocol-reverse-engineering-via-dynamic-inference/) - DynPRE starts from captured client–server traces and then interacts with a live protocol server to infer message formats and types. <sub>NDSS 2024 · Conference paper · Zhengxiong Luo et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2024-83-paper.pdf) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-dynpre/)</sub>
- [**Lifting Network Protocol Implementation to Precise Format Specification with Security Applications**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3576915.3616614) - NetLifter statically lifts source-available C protocol parsers into BNF-style message grammars and first-order constraints between packet fields. <sub>ACM CCS 2023 · Conference paper · Qingkai Shi et al. · [PDF](https://qingkaishi.github.io/public_pdfs/CCS23.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/qingkaishi/netlifter) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-netlifter/)</sub>
- [**Extracting Protocol Format as State Machine via Controlled Static Loop Analysis**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13483) - The paper extracts protocol message formats from parser code by analyzing parsing loops as state machines. <sub>arXiv 2023 · Preprint · Qingkai Shi et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.13483) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-protocol-format-state-machine/)</sub>
- [**BinaryInferno: A Semantic-Driven Approach to Field Inference for Binary Message Formats**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/binaryinferno-a-semantic-driven-approach-to-field-inference-for-binary-message-formats/) - Infers partial binary-message formats from static message samples without instrumenting an executable. <sub>NDSS 2023 · Conference paper · Jared Chandler et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/ndss2023_s131_paper.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/binaryinferno/binaryinferno) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-binaryinferno/)</sub>
- [**The Closer You Look, The More You Learn: A Grey-box Approach to Protocol State Machine Learning**](https://doi.org/10.1145/3548606.3559365) - StateInspector learns protocol Mealy machines by combining active message queries with snapshots of runtime memory, without requiring the target’s source code. <sub>ACM CCS 2022 · Conference paper · Chris McMahon Stone et al. · [PDF](https://tomchothia.gitlab.io/Papers/greyboxstatelearning_ccs2022.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/ChrisMcMStone/state-inspector) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-stateinspector/)</sub>
- [**Fingerprinting and analysis of Bluetooth devices with automata learning**](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10703-023-00425-y) - Learns Mealy-machine models of Bluetooth Low Energy implementations on physical peripherals by active automata learning. <sub>Formal Methods in System Design 2022 · Journal article · Andrea Pferscher et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.16074v2) · [Code](https://github.com/apferscher/ble-learning) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-ble-automata-learning/)</sub>
- [**Automated Attack Synthesis by Extracting Finite State Machines from Protocol Specification Documents**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.09470) - Extracts protocol FSMs from RFC prose using technical word representations, zero-shot text mapping, and rules, then uses the extracted FSMs to synthesize attacks. <sub>IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2022 · Conference accepted · Maria Leonor Pacheco et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2202.09470) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-attack-synthesis-fsm/)</sub>
- [**Noncompliance as Deviant Behavior: An Automated Black-box Noncompliance Checker for 4G LTE Cellular Devices**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3460120.3485388) - DIKEUE checks 4G LTE control-plane (NAS and RRC) implementations in commercial phones and modems for noncompliance through differential testing rather than predefined security properties. <sub>ACM CCS 2021 · Conference paper · Syed Rafiul Hussain et al. · [PDF](https://syed-rafiul-hussain.github.io/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/dikeue.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/SyNSec-den/DIKEUE/tree/5975807883265e275ef533f18a0c21b56e3b4e8a) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-dikeue/)</sub>
- [**NetPlier: Probabilistic Network Protocol Reverse Engineering from Message Traces**](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/netplier-probabilistic-network-protocol-reverse-engineering-from-message-traces/) - Uses multiple sequence alignment and probabilistic keyword-field inference to cluster network messages by type, evaluated across ten protocols with downstream format and state-machine analysis. <sub>NDSS 2021 · Conference paper · Yapeng Ye et al. · [PDF](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/ndss2021_4A-5_24531_paper.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/yapengye/NetPlier) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-netplier/)</sub>
- [**Message Type Identification of Binary Network Protocols using Continuous Segment Similarity**](https://doi.org/10.1109/infocom41043.2020.9155275) - The method compares field-based feature vectors, combines Hirschberg alignment with DBSCAN, and configures its parameters automatically. <sub>IEEE INFOCOM 2020 - IEEE Conference on Computer Communications · Conference paper · Stephan Kleber et al. · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.03391) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-message-type-identification-of-binary-network/)</sub>
- [**LibreCAN: Automated CAN Message Translator**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3319535.3363190) - LibreCAN reverse-engineers proprietary CAN message formats from traffic recorded at a vehicle's OBD-II port, without the OEM's DBC translation files. <sub>ACM CCS 2019 · Conference paper · Mert D. Pesé et al. · [PDF](https://rtcl.eecs.umich.edu/rtclweb/assets/publications/2019/fv075-peseA.pdf) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-librecan/)</sub>
- [**Automatic Wireless Protocol Reverse Engineering**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/woot19/presentation/pohl) - Infers message formats of proprietary wireless protocols from demodulated physical-layer captures: it aligns messages by preamble and sync word, then uses RSSI and dedicated engines to label length, address, sequence-number and checksum fields, optionally using known addresses or field positions. <sub>13th USENIX Workshop on Offensive Technologies (WOOT 19) 2019 · Conference paper · Johannes Pohl et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/woot19-paper_pohl.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/jopohl/urh) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-wireless-protocol-re/)</sub>
- [**NEMESYS: Network Message Syntax Reverse Engineering by Analysis of the Intrinsic Structure of Individual Messages**](https://www.usenix.org/conference/woot18/presentation/kleber) - Infers approximate field boundaries within individual binary-protocol messages from changes in bit congruence, and introduces Format Match Score to compare inferred segmentation with known protocol dissectors. <sub>12th USENIX Workshop on Offensive Technologies (WOOT 18) 2018 · Conference paper · Stephan Kleber et al. · [PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/conference/woot18/woot18-paper-kleber.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/vs-uulm/nemesys) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-nemesys/)</sub>
- [**Dissecting Customized Protocols: Automatic Analysis for Customized Protocols based on IEEE 802.15.4**](https://doi.org/10.1145/2939918.2939921) - WASp groups captured packets, reconstructs customized IEEE 802.15.4 protocols to byte-level accuracy, and generates packets for verification or spoofing. <sub>WiSec'16 2016 · Conference paper · Kibum Choi et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/2939918.2939921) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-dissecting-customized-protocols/)</sub>
- [**A Survey of Automatic Protocol Reverse Engineering Tools**](https://doi.org/10.1145/2840724) - Surveys automatic tools for reverse engineering closed network protocols and organizes them by whether they recover protocol state machines or message formats. <sub>ACM Computing Surveys 2015 · Journal article · John Narayan et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/2840724) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-protocol-re-tools-survey/)</sub>
- [**AUTOPROBE: Towards Automatic Active Malicious Server Probing Using Dynamic Binary Analysis**](https://doi.org/10.1145/2660267.2660352) - Autoprobe analyzes malware binaries to generate C&amp;C server fingerprints, including for pull-based protocols and servers offline during fingerprint generation. <sub>CCS'14 2014 · Conference paper · Zhaoyan Xu et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/2660267.2660352) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-autoprobe/)</sub>
- [**Towards Automated Protocol Reverse Engineering Using Semantic Information**](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2590296.2590346) - Infers the vocabulary of an undocumented protocol, its message types and formats, from communication traces. <sub>ACM ASIA CCS 2014 · Conference paper · Georges Bossert et al. · [PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/2590296.2590346) · [Code](https://github.com/netzob/netzob) · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/papers/paper-netzob/)</sub>
